title: Oklahoma 14, Kansas 10: The Nov. 18, 1967 Comeback in Norman
question: What happened when Oklahoma played Kansas on November 18, 1967?
answer: No. 7 Oklahoma beat Kansas 14-10 at Norman on November 18, 1967, scoring the final touchdown in the fourth quarter after trailing 10-7 entering the period. The win kept the Sooners unbeaten in Big Eight play on the way to a conference title.
summary: On November 18, 1967, No. 7 Oklahoma rallied past Kansas 14-10 in Norman, a late-season escape on the way to the Big Eight title and an Orange Bowl win.
body: Fans who love Sooner history will find a gritty, easy-to-miss date on the calendar: November 18, 1967. That afternoon, seventh-ranked Oklahoma (6-1) hosted Kansas (4-4) at Owen Field, with 57,649 on hand according to the SoonerStats box score.

Kansas struck first with a field goal in the opening quarter and led 3-0 at halftime. Each team scored a touchdown in the third quarter, so the Jayhawks carried a 10-7 lead into the final period. Oklahoma then found the end zone in the fourth quarter for the 14-10 final. The box score lists the points by quarter but not the scorers, so this post leaves those plays out.

The numbers show how tight it was. Kansas outgained the Sooners on the ground, 197 yards to 100, while Oklahoma threw for 129 yards on 12 of 23 passing and committed two interceptions. Kansas had no turnovers, and OU still won by four.

The result mattered. Oklahoma finished 7-0 in Big Eight play and is listed as the conference champion, and the Sooners closed the regular season with a 21-14 win at Nebraska on November 23. They then beat Tennessee 26-24 in the Orange Bowl on January 1, 1968, entering that game ranked third. A narrow November afternoon like this one was part of how that season stayed on track.
